content: 1. Both aripiprazole and gemifloxacin are known to prolong the QTc interval. It is recommended to use these medications with caution and monitor the patient closely. 2. Atomoxetine and gemifloxacin both increase the QTc interval. Caution is advised, and monitoring is necessary. 3. Azithromycin can enhance the toxicity of gemifloxacin by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor the patient. 4. Gemifloxacin reduces the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 5. Co-administration of gemifloxacin and bedaquiline increases the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring, including ECG, are recommended. 6. Betamethasone and gemifloxacin together increase the risk of other adverse effects (see comment). Use caution and monitor. Co-administration of quinolone antibiotics and corticosteroids may increase the risk of tendon rupture. 7. Calcium acetate and gemifloxacin can mutually decrease each other's levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution, monitor, and separate administration by 2 hours. 8. Calcium carbonate and gemifloxacin can mutually decrease each other's levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution, monitor, and separate administration by 2 hours. 9. At the maximum recommended dose, deutetrabenazine does not prolong the QT interval to a clinically significant extent. However, certain conditions may increase the risk of torsades de pointes or sudden death when using QT-prolonging drugs (e.g., bradycardia, hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia, co-administration with other QT-prolonging drugs, or congenital QT prolongation). Use caution and monitor the patient. Slight and transient QT prolongation has been observed with ezogabine, particularly when titrated to 1200 mg/day. QT interval monitoring is recommended when ezogabine is prescribed with agents known to prolong the QT interval. 45.
